visual.general_description: Flowchart of a treatment algorithm for catatonia built from rounded boxes and block arrows.
visual.detailed_description: Blue-outlined rounded boxes connected by blue block arrows form a top-to-bottom flowchart on a white background. Top row: a central box reading "Suspected catatonia with 3 or more features"; a left arrow labelled "Unclear" points to a box reading "Lorazepam Challenge"; a right arrow labelled "No" points to a box reading "Consider alternate diagnoses"; a downward arrow labelled "Yes" leads to the large central box. The large central box is headed "Assessment in secondary care" and lists: history and collateral history; physical examination; use validated catatonia instrument (e.g. BFCRS/PCRS); consider appropriate legal framework where patient is unable to make decisions; investigations (blood tests, urine drug screen, lumbar puncture, EEG, neuroimaging) with two diamond-bulleted sub-items (if 1st episode or unclear diagnosis: consider neuroimaging and autoantibodies in serum and CSF; if risk factors for seizures or encephalitis: consider EEG with continuous monitoring if possible); and lorazepam challenge (if not performed above). The printed spelling "Neuroimagin" and "continous" is as shown. A downward arrow leads to a box reading "Prompt treatment" with italic text "not always necessary to wait results of investigations sent"; a left arrow leads to a box reading "Treat underlying disorder" with italic text "if antipsychotics used, prescribe with caution"; a right arrow leads to a box reading "Prevent and manage complications". A downward arrow from "Prompt treatment" leads to a box reading "Lorazepam and/ or ECT", then to "Re-evaluate diagnosis", then to "NMDA receptor antagonist". A separate rounded box at lower right headed "Special cases" lists six bulleted entries with bold condition names followed by actions with arrows: antipsychotic-induced catatonia (stop antipsychotic to benzodiazepine); benzodiazepine withdrawal catatonia (restart benzodiazepine); chronic, mild catatonia in schizophrenia (clozapine trial); clozapine withdrawal catatonia (restart clozapine to ECT); malignant catatonia (stop dopamine antagonists to lorazepam to ECT); NMS (stop dopamine antagonists and anticholinergics to supportive medical care).
